title: Operating and cooperating grace, taken with the later Thomists
source_text: XX. Caeterum non improbant Scholae Reformatae Doctores quod Scholastici gratiam distinguunt in Operantem & cooperantem. Sed cum Thomistis recentioribus per gratiam Operantem intelligi volunt illam per quam aliquis primum ad Deum convertitur: per cooperantem vero illam per quam aliquis jam ad Deum conversus ad bene agendum movetur. Sic Aretius loco supra citato, Gratia, inquit, alias est operans, alias cooperans. Illa dicitur voluntatem nostram sanare & mutare in melius. Haec mutatam confirmat, & ut recte agat efficit.
pass_a_gloss: XX. However the Doctors of the Reformed School do not disapprove that the Scholastics distinguish grace into Operating and cooperating. But with the more recent Thomists they will have understood by Operating grace that by which someone is first converted to God: but by cooperating that by which someone already converted to God is moved to acting well. Thus Aretius in the place cited above, Grace, he says, is at one time operating, at another cooperating. The former is said to heal our will and change it for the better. The latter confirms it changed, and effects that it act rightly.
pass_b_english: Thesis XX. The doctors of the Reformed school do not object to the scholastics' distinction of grace into operating and cooperating grace. But, with the more recent Thomists, they take operating grace to be the grace by which a person is first converted to God, and cooperating grace to be the grace by which someone already converted to God is moved to act well.

So Aretius, at the place cited above: Grace, he says, is sometimes operating and sometimes cooperating. The first is said to heal our will and change it for the better; the second strengthens the will once changed and brings it about that it acts rightly.
